title: The Counter‑Reformation
key_facts: Catholic reform movement responding to Protestant challenges
Council of Trent (1545–1563) defined doctrine and discipline
New religious orders (Jesuits) led education and missions
causes: Spread of Protestantism and calls for Church reform
Need to clarify doctrine and improve clerical standards
Competition for influence among European states
outcome: Doctrinal clarification and seminaries for priestly training
Revitalized Catholic spirituality, art, and education
impacts: Global Catholic missions and education networks
Baroque culture and art as instruments of devotion
